benefits.title: Vacuum, never a purge
benefits.description: Many installers release refrigerant to push air out of the lines. We connect a vacuum pump and evacuate the circuit before commissioning, so moisture and air never reach the compressor — the single biggest factor in how long your AC lives.

benefits.title: Raised in the trade

benefits.title: Per-foot billing you can watch

benefits.title: Placed for Chennai, not a manual

faqs.question: Why does vacuuming matter if brand installers just purge the lines?
faqs.answer: Purging pushes air out by releasing refrigerant, and it leaves moisture behind. Moisture inside an R32 or R410A circuit forms acids that quietly attack the compressor. We connect a vacuum pump and pull the lines down before releasing gas. It takes longer, and it is the difference between an AC that cools for a season and one that cools for years.

faqs.question: How is copper piping charged?
faqs.answer: The core price covers the installation itself; insulated copper pair coil is billed at ₹200-300 per foot depending on tonnage. We measure the run with you before work starts, and the exact footage appears on your digital invoice. You are never rounded up to the nearest coil.

faqs.question: Which wall should the indoor and outdoor units go on?
faqs.answer: Indoors, we pick a wall that throws air along the length of the room and can genuinely carry the unit's weight. Outdoors, shade matters in Chennai's 40°C summers, and near the coast we avoid direct sea-facing exposure where possible because salt air corrodes the condenser coil. We also insist on service clearance, so future maintenance does not need scaffolding.

faqs.question: Do I need a stabilizer in Chennai?
faqs.answer: Many modern inverter ACs tolerate a wide voltage band, but Chennai's fluctuations — especially in older buildings and at peak summer load — can still exceed it. We measure your supply voltage during the visit and tell you plainly whether your specific unit needs protection. If it does not, we would rather you skip the purchase.

faqs.question: How long does an installation take, and can it happen today?
faqs.answer: A standard split installation takes around two to three hours on site; long piping runs or core-drilling through RCC add time, which we flag upfront. Same-day slots are available, and in covered areas a technician can reach you in 60-90 minutes.
